bull.b: Very strong TPV growth combined with 140% net revenue retention indicates that DLocal is expanding both transaction volumes and existing merchant relationships. This supports durable revenue compounding through deeper wallet share, broader payment adoption, and recurring usage across its emerging-market network.

Expanded licensing across 26 markets strengthens DLocal’s ability to serve global merchants through a single integration while supporting local compliance and payment access. Regulatory coverage can raise entry barriers, improve customer confidence, and enable sustained geographic and product expansion.

Minimal leverage limits financial risk and preserves flexibility to invest in technology, licenses, product expansion, and new markets without depending heavily on debt. Strong returns on equity also indicate that the company is using its capital base efficiently while remaining financially resilient.

bear.b: The decline in gross and net margins shows that revenue growth has not translated proportionally into profitability over time. If this pattern persists, DLocal may have less operating leverage and reduced capacity to convert expanding payment volumes into durable earnings and cash flow.

Ongoing take-rate compression can structurally reduce revenue captured from each payment dollar even when TPV grows rapidly. Higher processing costs and lower pricing tiers, particularly in Mexico, create additional pressure on unit economics and make sustained margin expansion more difficult.

Recent cash generation is strong, yet the prior negative cash-flow year reveals meaningful variability in conversion from earnings to cash. Such swings can reflect working-capital or timing effects and may make internally funded investment and capital returns less predictable across reporting periods.
